title: How long is a rectangle made of two identical squares?
description: A rectangle is built from two identical squares placed side by side, using a perpendicular and the compass to copy the side length. When the side of the first square is four centimetres, the whole length of the rectangle is found. Keeko's doubt is that the length is also four centimetres.
teaching_notes: One idea: a rectangle made of two identical squares is as long as two square sides, and the compass copies the same side length beyond the first square. Watch for students who stop at the first square and give the side as the whole length.

source: Construct a rectangle ACDF that can be divided into two iden
video_script.why: A learner constructs a rectangle that splits into two identical squares and finds its length from the side of one square.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rectangle ACDF split into the squares ABEF and BCDE, with AF four centimetres
video_script.anchor: a rectangle ACDF with a line BE splitting it into two identical squares
video_script.wrong_answer: eigh cee is also four centimetres, the same as eigh eff
video_script.wrong_move: reads the side of the first square as the whole length of the rectangle
video_script.payoff_line: The length is two square sides.

final_answer.value: AC = 8 cm. The rectangle is 8 cm by 4 cm

maths_rules: AF = AB = BE = FE = BC = CD = ED = 4 cm (all the short lines are equal)
perpendicular at A, with the compass tip at A and radius AF marking B
same radius from B marking C, so BC = 4 cm
AC = AB + BC = 4 cm + 4 cm = 8 cm; the rectangle is 8 cm by 4 cm
video_script.design: The first square is drawn, the same radius is copied beyond it, and the rectangle is completed and measured.

beats.on_screen: title card, then a rectangle ACDF with a line BE splitting it into two squares, and AF marked

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the rectangle is drawn
marks.ask: the line bee ee appears and AF is marked 4 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a construction from your book.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>A rectangle eigh cee dee eff is cut into two identical squares, and eigh eff is four centimetres. How long must eigh cee be?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: two identical squares ABEF and BCDE side by side, sharing the side BE

marks.same: all the short lines are marked with matching ticks
marks.share: the shared side bee ee glows

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Identical squares have equal sides, so all the short lines in the figure are equal.
<bookmark mark='share'/>The two squares share one side, bee ee, and the rectangle is built from them.

beats.on_screen: Given: rectangle ACDF = squares ABEF and BCDE; AF = 4 cm
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a rectangle made of two identical squares, with eigh eff four centimetres.

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the length of eigh cee.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: draw AF = 4 cm, the side of the first square

marks.af: AF is drawn and labelled 4 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='af'/>Step one, draw eigh eff equal to four centimetres, the side of the first square.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: draw a perpendicular at A; compass tip at A, radius AF, mark B; AB = 4 cm

marks.arc: the compass arc cuts it at B, and AB is labelled 4 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='perp'/>Step two, draw a perpendicular at eigh.
<bookmark mark='arc'/>Put the compass tip at eigh with radius eigh eff, and mark bee. Eigh bee is four centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: same radius from B, mark C beyond B; BC = 4 cm

marks.copy: the compass keeps its opening and marks C beyond B, and BC is labelled 4 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='copy'/>Step three, keep the same radius, and mark cee beyond bee. Bee cee is another four centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: repeat at F to place E and D, and join D to C; AC = AB + BC

marks.rep: the same two marks are made from F to place E and D
marks.join: D is joined to C and the rectangle is complete

narration: <bookmark mark='rep'/>Step four, repeat the same marks at eff to place ee and dee.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Join dee to cee, and the rectangle is complete.

beats.on_screen: Answer: AC = 4 cm + 4 cm = 8 cm; the rectangle is 8 cm by 4 cm

marks.res: AB and BC are added along AC

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The length is two square sides.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Four centimetres and four centimetres together make eight centimetres, so eigh cee is eight centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the finished rectangle
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: AC labelled 4 cm is struck out; AB and BC are traced separately, then together along AC

marks.doubt: AC is labelled 4 cm beside AF
marks.fix: AB is traced as the first square side
marks.keep: BC is traced after it and AC is traced as both together

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks eigh cee is also four centimetres, the same as eigh eff.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But eigh eff is a side of the first square only.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Eigh cee runs along both squares, so it holds two sides of four centimetres each.
